shared_elements: horizontal line of incised/pecked script-like signs
shallow carving directly onto an irregular natural rock face
repeated small strokes and angular sign-forms
justification: Both surfaces depict nothing figural at all but rather sequences of small abstract linear signs set out in horizontal registers on a natural rock face, a fairly specific shared scheme of writing rather than imagery. The main difference is density and organisation: A carries a single isolated line of signs on an otherwise blank face, while B is packed with many superimposed parallel lines covering the whole surface, and the individual sign shapes (loops and curves in B versus predominantly vertical strokes in A) are not evidently the same repertoire.
